research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.
research_basis.licence_handling: Original implementation content informed by Jisc AI maturity structure. Scenarios and practitioner language are independently written to avoid reproducing Jisc wording.

mappings.target_construct: Governance & Human Commitment: Governance & Risk Management; Leadership & Capability
what_transfers: institutional AI leadership, governance, and strategic direction
what_does_not_transfer: QS's broader external branding and capability positioning elements
mappings.rationale: This is the closest peer mapping for institutional AI strategy and leadership.

mappings.target_construct: Governance & Human Commitment: Leadership & Capability; faculty and administrative capability enablers
what_transfers: AI skills, capacity building, and organisational readiness
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's explicit tertiary-sector role-based literacy language
mappings.rationale: Both frameworks treat capability building as central to sustainable AI maturity.

mappings.target_construct: Outreach & Operational Efficiency; Teaching, Learning & Assessment; Research & Scholarship enablers
what_transfers: technical capability, infrastructure, workflow support, and operationalisation
what_does_not_transfer: QS distributes infrastructure implications across pillars rather than holding one standalone technical dimension
mappings.rationale: The overlap is strong but structurally distributed in QS.

mappings.target_construct: Governance & Human Commitment: Code of Conduct & Privacy Protection; Governance & Risk Management
what_transfers: data governance, readiness, and protection for AI use
what_does_not_transfer: QS does not foreground data readiness as a separate top-level dimension
mappings.rationale: Jisc is more explicit about data foundations as a dependency.

mappings.target_construct: Governance & Human Commitment: Regulatory & Ethical Standards; Code of Conduct & Privacy Protection
what_transfers: responsible AI, ethics, privacy, oversight, and accountability
what_does_not_transfer: some broader sector-positioning and assessment-process elements in QS
mappings.rationale: This is a close conceptual match.

mappings.target_construct: Strategy across all pillars; Planning & Governance child dimensions
what_transfers: strategic direction, governance ownership, and alignment to mission
what_does_not_transfer: THE DMI is digital-wide rather than AI-specific
mappings.rationale: AI strategy is a domain-specific extension of the broader strategy construct in THE DMI.

what_transfers: skills, confidence, adoption readiness, and cultural support
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific literacy and specialised capability content

what_transfers: infrastructure, integration, resilience, and service readiness
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific lifecycle and model monitoring concerns
mappings.rationale: Technology maturity maps directly, with AI-specific details added on the Jisc side.

what_transfers: data governance, availability, and evidence capability
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific dataset readiness and model-use constraints
mappings.rationale: This is one of the clearest cross-framework matches.

mappings.target_construct: Strategy + Data + Utilisation dependency pattern; Planning & Governance
what_does_not_transfer: THE DMI has no dedicated ethics dimension
mappings.rationale: THE captures responsible use indirectly, while Jisc AI maturity makes it explicit.

mappings.target_construct: Organisational Digital Culture / Knowledge Management & Use / Knowledge Exchange & Partnerships
what_transfers: strategic alignment and leadership for transformation
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific governance and risk management detail
mappings.rationale: AI strategy builds on wider digital maturity but adds domain-specific governance.

what_transfers: capability growth, confidence, and cultural adoption
what_does_not_transfer: AI-specific literacy, prompt use, and specialist support
mappings.rationale: This is the strongest sibling bridge.

mappings.target_construct: Knowledge Creation & Innovation / Knowledge Management & Use
what_does_not_transfer: AI model lifecycle and managed-service details
mappings.rationale: Digital maturity provides the broader substrate; AI maturity narrows the focus.

mappings.target_construct: Guidance for generative AI in education and research: data privacy, regulation, and human-centred governance
what_transfers: data protection, validation, governance, and readiness concerns
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's institution-level operational detail and stage model
mappings.rationale: UNESCO guidance strongly reinforces data privacy and governance expectations for AI in education.

mappings.target_construct: Guidance for generative AI in education and research: ethical validation, human-centred regulation, equity, and meaningful use
what_transfers: human-centred, ethical, safe, equitable, and accountable AI use
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's specific maturity staging and UK-tertiary operational focus
mappings.rationale: This is a strong normative mapping, with Jisc supplying maturity staging.

mappings.target_construct: AI and education: guidance for policy-makers; human-centred policy response
what_transfers: strategic planning, policy response, and institutional readiness
what_does_not_transfer: Jisc's operational tertiary-education maturity model structure
mappings.rationale: UNESCO informs the policy lens, while Jisc supplies a staged maturity implementation frame.
